entries.test: Public reporting of major disruptions attributable to Mythos between its April controlled release and June 9, 2026 would establish whether the described catastrophes occurred.
entries.note: In context, 'the world has not ended' refers to the catastrophic outcomes described earlier.

entries.test: Anthropic's release announcements and contemporaneous reports of companies imposing token budgets would establish the claimed timing.
entries.note: The passage juxtaposes developments; it does not establish falling aggregate demand or assert business pressure as the cause.

entries.test: Public company policies and reporting on AI spending through June 9, 2026 would show whether unrestricted token consumption was giving way to token budgets.
entries.note: The budget clause supplies a concrete reading of the otherwise informal 'tokenmaxxing' claim.

entries.test: Anthropic's release documentation, safeguards disclosures, and access terms would establish whether Mythos became broadly available after guardrails were added.
entries.note: Broad availability is supported by the following paragraph. 'Only' adds an exclusion of other changes that the source does not explicitly assert.
The prediction is qualified by 'probably' and depends on unilateral action or China's continued existence.

entries.test: Anthropic's historical public commitments, new-model release announcement, and published benchmark comparisons would establish the claimed reversal and competitive positioning.
entries.note: 'Meant to beat everyone' strengthens 'racing everyone,' while omitting the source's 'all the benchmarks' scope. The historical commitment is Marcus's own assertion about Anthropic.

entries.test: Anthropic's publicity materials, documented media briefings, and subsequent coverage and public reactions would show whether its danger messaging shaped credulous reporting and belief.
entries.note: The metaphor has a concrete contextual allegation: successful manipulation of coverage about Mythos's dangers.

entries.test: GPT-2 and subsequent model announcements, associated media coverage, release histories, and the named individuals' documented roles would establish whether the danger-publicity-release sequence recurred from 2019 through June 2026.
entries.note: The claim concerns a recurring sequence involving the named former OpenAI personnel, rather than Anthropic operating throughout all seven years.
